elaine: Quick question — thinking about making the left rail fully collapsible but keeping a persistent breadcrumb bar above the main canvas so deep links always surface the full path. Sketch: https://figma.com/s/console-nav-proto. Does that break permalinks or keyboard flow?

marta: I like the persistence but keyboard users need a predictable tab order. If breadcrumbs are always present they must be first tabbable element after the global nav. Also we should expose a "Skip to main" link.

peter: Routing question: current canonical resource URLs look like `/org/:orgId/workspaces/:wsId/models/:modelId`. If we collapse groups in the rail, we can't rely on rail state to reconstruct the path. We should encode the full resource path in the URL and treat rail state as UI-only.

sam: Implementation note — using hash anchors for panels (`#metrics`) made browser restore/back weird in the canary. I suggest we prefer a query param for subpanels, e.g. `?panel=metrics` or a nested path like `/models/:id/metrics`.

kevin: Accessibility nit: mark the active crumb with `aria-current=\"page\"` and when the breadcrumb bar expands/collapses announce that with an `aria-live=\"polite\"` region. Also ensure collapsible groups expose `aria-expanded` and keyboard handlers (Enter/Space).

design-bot: Prototype preview deployed: https://staging.redwood/console/nav-proto (build 502). Tester notes: requires Chrome >= 114 for the continuous-scroll behavior.

marta: :thumbsup: Also recommend adding a small visible focus ring on the crumbs (high contrast) and a dedicated skip link for screenreader users.

peter: Edge-case: links shared from older UI (old query params like `?panel=overview&view=compact`) need a router-level redirect mapping to the new path. Otherwise team pages will 404.

elaine: Proposed decision (for quick sync):
1) Breadcrumb bar remains persistent and canonicalizes resource path. URLs are the source of truth.
2) Left rail becomes collapsible; collapse state is stored in user prefs and can be overridden by `?rail=collapsed` in URL for shared links.
3) Deep links use path-first approach: resource paths for primary entities, `?panel=` for subviews. Avoid hash anchors for new routes.
4) A11y: `aria-current`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-live` announcements, and a visible skip-to-content link.

Vote: sam: +1, peter: +1, marta: :raised_hand: (need to validate mobile/compact behavior), kevin: +1.

elaine: Thanks — I'll draft the RFC + tickets: router mapping, redirect table for legacy params, a11y checklist. Assigning dev impl to @peter and a11y sign-off to @kevin. Will post PR link once ready.
